provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Int family batch. Craft-driven, mostly Instagram-only setters; copy leans on layout, waterproofing and grout lines. No tile, membrane or grout brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Sheet and liquid membranes, mortar-bed versus foam shower pans, flood testing before tile, curbless entries, niches and benches built watertight
pageStructurePlus.why: A shower leak behind tile is the failure every buyer fears. Showing the waterproofing step is how a careful setter beats a cheaper bid.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Herringbone, stacked, offset, chevron and basketweave layouts, large-format porcelain, zellige and mosaic, and how the layout is centred around niches, windows and outlets
pageStructurePlus.why: Tile buyers decide by pattern first and material second. A layout gallery lets them point at exactly what they want.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Grout colour and joint width, cement versus epoxy grout, metal edge profiles versus bullnose, and caulk at every change of plane
pageStructurePlus.why: The finish details are what separates a tile setter from a handyman. Buyers who care about clean edges pay for someone who explains them.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Removing an old backsplash without chipping the countertop, outlet extenders, under-cabinet lighting, how long a kitchen backsplash takes, and when grout can be wiped
pageStructurePlus.why: Backsplashes are a small, quick decision. A page that makes install day look easy turns a browser into a booked date.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Bringing your own tile, how much overage to order, checking boxes for lot and shade before install, lippage on handmade tile, and what the setter can't warranty
pageStructurePlus.why: Most tile buyers have already fallen for a tile at a showroom. A clear policy answers the first question they ask and prevents the worst callback.

designDirections.name: Wet Saw

designDirections.name: Grout Line
designDirections.bestFor: Setters with a strong Instagram grid of showers, patterns and niches that needs a proper home

designDirections.name: Stone Gallery
designDirections.bestFor: High-end setters doing book-matched slabs, zellige walls and steam showers for designers

designDirections.whyItFits: Gallery white with a Didone display steps back so marble veining and handmade glaze carry the page, the way a designer's portfolio does.

openers.line: Searched tile installers in {City} and your listing came up with great reviews but no website. A buyer picking a shower setter wants to see niches and grout lines before they call.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a tile buyer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your tile work lives entirely on Instagram. It's gorgeous, but nobody can search a herringbone backsplash in {City} and land on a grid, and there's nowhere to ask for a quote.
openers.hook: Check the bio link and the Maps listing. If both point to Instagram or nothing, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Your tile grid with a quote form built in: {demo-link}

openers.line: The tile site on your listing still has a free-host banner and the newest shower on it is a few years old. Your grid shows much better tilework than that.
openers.hook: Open the site and compare its newest job with their newest post. Note the gap.
openers.linkLine: Your newest tilework on a current site: {demo-link}

openers.line: On a phone your site crops every shower photo to a strip, so the pattern and the niche disappear. Tile is the one trade where the close-up does the selling.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your tile gallery, full-height on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most backsplash quotes start with a photo of the wall and the tile someone picked. Right now that means DMs and texts, and the details get lost between them.
openers.hook: Check for any form. If quotes only happen through DMs or calls, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A tile quote form that takes wall photos and the tile choice: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've set herringbone, stacked and chevron in the last few months, and they're scattered across the grid. Sorted by pattern, a buyer could point and say 'that one'.
openers.hook: Count how many different tile patterns appear on their grid. Name two if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your tile jobs sorted by pattern: {demo-link}

openers.line: Reviews about a shower that's never leaked and grout lines you could set a ruler on are buried on your listing. They should sit right under the tile photos.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about leaks, grout or patience. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the tile they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: October is when people want a new kitchen backsplash before hosting. Tile setters who show up in that search fill November in a week.
openers.hook: Use this in September and October. Name the holiday in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready for the pre-holiday backsplash rush: {demo-link}

openers.line: Tile customers message at midnight with a showroom photo and 'how much for this?'. A quote form with fields for wall size and tile choice answers half of that while you sleep.
openers.hook: Look at their comments for price questions left unanswered. If you find a few, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A tile quote request that works while you sleep: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a tile helper. A good apprentice wants to see what kind of tile work they'd learn on, and a real site shows that better than a story.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A tile site with a page for helpers and apprentices: {demo-link}

openers.line: You tile showers across {City}, but someone in {Neighborhood} searching 'shower tile near me' has no page telling them you'll come out there.
openers.hook: Find towns named in captions or tags. Use the one most often tagged.
openers.linkLine: A tile page for each town you work in: {demo-link}

openers.line: Half your tile clients probably arrive with tile already bought. A page that explains overage, checking lots and what you can warranty would save you that phone call every week.
openers.hook: Look for comments or captions mentioning tile the client picked. If you see any, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A bring-your-own-tile page, written for your setters: {demo-link}

openers.line: People hiring for a shower are scared of a leak behind the tile. A page that shows your waterproofing and flood test answers that before they ask.
openers.hook: Look for any post showing membrane or a flood test. If they have one, mention it.
openers.linkLine: Shower waterproofing explained on one tile page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Looks like designers tag you on some of these bathrooms. When a designer sends a client your way, the first thing that client does is search for a tile site.
openers.hook: Find a designer or contractor tag on their posts. Name them if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where a designer's tile referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: The {specific recent job} on your grid has the cleanest niche I've seen this month. A tile job like that deserves to be the first thing a buyer sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished shower or backsplash and name it: tile, pattern and room.
openers.linkLine: That tile job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner}, that {specific recent job} on your grid is beautiful tile work.

I was looking for tile setters in {City} and found {Business Name} on Instagram, but no site where someone can browse by pattern or send a quote request with their wall measurements. I put together a sample tile site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, bumping this in case it got buried under tile DMs. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a gallery sorted by pattern, a shower waterproofing page, and a quote form that takes wall photos and the tile they picked. If it's not your thing, say so and I'll drop it.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for tile setters here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did you see it?"

IF NO:
"All good. Short version: I built a sample tile site for {Business Name}, with your kind of work sorted by pattern, a shower waterproofing page and a quote form that takes photos, plus marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many pattern and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a setter your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, roughly one backsplash."
"Can I show you around it for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday after you're off the job?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice, and pull your best showers off the grid with you."

objections.handler: "Instagram is a great portfolio for people who already follow you. A stranger searching 'shower tile installer' in {City} lands on Google, not your grid. The site catches them and sends them back to it."
"Then the site lets you choose. Showers and feature walls over small patch jobs, and a waitlist form so you don't lose the good ones."

objections.objection: The contractors I sub for give me enough work.
objections.handler: "That's steady until one of them slows down. A site gets you direct shower jobs where you set the price, not the general."

objections.objection: People just want the cheapest tile guy.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the ones who've seen a shower leak or a lippy floor. Your waterproofing and layout is what they're paying for."

objections.objection: I don't have time to write anything.
objections.handler: "You don't. I write it from your captions and a ten-minute call, and you approve it. The tile photos do most of the talking anyway."
"{Build Range}. For you it'd be about {Build Price}, a pattern gallery, a quote form and a shower page. Less than one tub surround."

email.subject: Tile site for {Business Name}

sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm pulling the {Business Name} tile demo down on Friday.

Want me to keep it up for you? One word is plenty.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, people are starting to plan holiday backsplashes and new-year bathrooms. Thought of you.

The tile site is still ready whenever you are, same price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one tub surround or a kitchen backsplash, never to an hourly rate. Setters think in jobs and square feet.
Price the gallery by finished tile jobs sorted by pattern and room, not by page count.
A quote form that takes wall photos, measurements and the chosen tile is the core of the site. Quote extra fields as their own line.
Only quote a shower waterproofing page for setters who build pans and membranes themselves.
Most setters are solo. Keep monthly add-ons small and skip anything that needs a dispatcher.
Pulling the best posts off their Instagram is real work. Price the gallery curation, don't throw it in.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has a layout explainer, grout notes and a dozen finished tile jobs in that pattern.

lineItems.item: Photo quote form with wall measurements
lineItems.description: Max with multiple photo uploads, a tile-already-bought field, a square-footage helper and a sketch field.
Max with step-by-step build photos from their own jobs and a flood-test section.
Max when there are many posts to sort, rename and caption by pattern, tile and room.
Max with an overage calculator and a printable box-check checklist for the homeowner.
Max when each town page gets its own finished tile jobs and a local review.

whatElseYouSell.name: Close-up tile shoot and short reels
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Raking light on a finished shower shows every flat tile and tight grout line. One shoot gives the gallery and a month of tile reels."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, the week they finish a shower or feature wall they love.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for tile jobs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your Instagram tile posts go onto the Google profile too, tagged by town, so the map listing stops looking empty next to your grid."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review ask after the grout cures
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Once the grout's cured and the shower's been used, the client gets a short text asking for a review. That's when they love the tile most."

whatElseYouSell.name: Designer and showroom lookbook
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A printed and digital lookbook of your best tile patterns for showrooms and designers to hand out. Your name on the counter where people choose tile."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the pattern gallery is full.

whatElseYouSell.name: Pre-holiday backsplash promotion
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short September push for a new backsplash before the holidays books the quick kitchen tile jobs that fill gaps between showers."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in August, run in September.

whatElseYouSell.name: Instagram content plan for tile reels
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Grout-wipe reels and layout timelapses already travel. A steady plan turns them into quote requests that link back to the site."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, for setters who already post often.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The tile shop where your clients pick their zellige sends people to setters every day. Introduce me and I'll build their find-a-setter page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Showrooms only sell tile that gets installed. A setter list on their site is something they'd pay to keep current.

withoutAI.route: Plumbers who set shower valves before the tile
withoutAI.whoPays: The plumber, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who sets the valves before you tile? I'll build their site, and your shower page links to theirs."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: The plumber and the setter share every shower. One introduction from the setter is a warm door.

withoutAI.route: Small bathroom remodelers who sub out tile
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The remodeler you tile for needs a site with a room gallery, and your showers are the best photos in it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Remodelers buy bigger sites than setters, and the tile sub's work is already their best proof.

withoutAI.route: Countertop fabricators who finish before the backsplash
withoutAI.whoPays: The fabricator, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The stone shop installs the counter and the homeowner asks who does backsplashes. A site for them with your name on it answers that."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Backsplash always follows counters. Both sides refer constantly.

withoutAI.whoPays: The glass company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Frameless glass goes on the shower right after you finish the tile. The glass installer needs a site and a shared gallery with you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same shower, consecutive trades, and both sell on the finished photo.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Designers who tag you on bathroom posts need a portfolio site, and your tilework is the hero shot in half of it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers buy on looks and already work with the setter.

withAI.route: Tile layout visualiser for the showroom
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers photograph their wall and see the showroom's tile in herringbone or stacked before they drive in."
withAI.whyItWorks: It brings shoppers in with a shortlist, which is what tile showrooms sell on.

withAI.route: Tile quantity and overage assistant for showroom staff
withAI.pitchLine: "Counter staff enter the wall sizes and pattern and get a box count with overage, so nobody runs short mid-shower."
withAI.whyItWorks: Short orders and mismatched lots cost showrooms reorders and goodwill. A tiny tool stops both.

withAI.route: Follow-up texts for the glass installer
withAI.pitchLine: "The glass installer who follows you loses shower door quotes to slow follow-up. Same follow-up setup you have, configured for them."
withAI.whyItWorks: It's a second build of something working, and the introduction came from a trusted client.

withAI.pitchLine: "The remodeler drops in walkthrough photos and gets a draft bathroom scope with tile square footage to send the setter."
withAI.whyItWorks: Remodelers write scopes every week. A drafted one saves an evening and routes tile work to one setter.

withAI.pitchLine: "The designer describes the bathroom and gets a tile spec with layout, grout colour, joint width and edge trim to edit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Clear specs mean fewer setter callbacks, which designers and setters both want.

withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners ask the plumber about valve heights and niche spacing before tile. A bot trained on the plumber's answers handles it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Rough-in questions slow every shower. The setter's notes on spacing make the bot better.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back while the thinset is wet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Can't pick up with thinset on your hands? The caller gets a text asking for the room, a wall photo and the tile they chose."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Tile job price estimator by wall and floor area
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick backsplash, tub surround or walk-in shower, enter the size and the tile type, and see a range before you DM the setter."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price per square foot by job type, prep add-ons and minimum job.

softwareAI.name: Caption-to-reply drafts for tile reviews and comments
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Reviews and 'how much for this shower?' comments get a drafted reply in your voice that names the tile and pattern. You tap approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs twenty past replies and their standard answer on pricing. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit-at-booking for tile jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The client pays a deposit when they book the tile date, and the balance link goes out when the grout's sealed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Wall-photo tile pattern preview
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The client uploads a photo of their backsplash wall and sees the tile in herringbone, stacked or offset before they commit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their common patterns and a set of finished jobs to check the previews against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Tile layout planner with centring and cuts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the wall, the niche and the tile size, and it lays out the grid so you see where the slivers land before you snap a line."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their layout rules and a few past walls with measured tile counts.

softwareAI.name: Night-time tile quote assistant for DMs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Midnight 'how much for this?' DMs get a reply that asks for the wall size, the tile and a photo, and books a quote visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar, job types and the questions they always ask. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Tile job schedule with cure times
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each shower is booked with membrane, flood test, set, grout and seal days, so you never schedule grout before the thinset's ready."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their cure times by product type and how they stack jobs.

softwareAI.name: Shower build photo log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Snap the membrane, the flood test and the pan at each step and it files them by client. If a shower ever leaks, you have the proof of what's behind the tile."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their shower build steps and a phone they'll actually use on the job.

softwareAI.name: Tile box and overage calculator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload the client's tile spec and wall sizes, and it drafts the box count with overage for pattern and cuts for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their overage rules by pattern and a few past orders to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Grout sealing reminder sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A year after the shower's done, the client gets a reminder to reseal the grout, with your booking link. Small repeat tile jobs from people who already trust you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a list of past tile jobs with dates and a sealing price.

softwareAI.name: Client page with tile selections and dates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The client confirms the tile, grout colour and layout on one page and sees the start date, so nothing changes the morning you show up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the schedule in place first.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on showers, grout and bringing your own tile
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can you install tile I already bought' and 'do I need epoxy grout' at midnight, from your own rules."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ, the tile policy and current lead time, updated monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Showroom referral tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which tile showroom and which designer sent each shower job, so you know who to thank and where the good work comes from."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a referral field on the form and a list of showrooms they work with.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by tile job type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether showers, backsplashes or floors actually pay best once membrane, thinset and your days are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs material receipts and days on site for a season of tile jobs.

softwareAI.name: Pattern page writer from captions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Your Instagram captions become a new pattern or tile page each month, like 'zellige backsplash care', and you approve it before it goes up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs access to their captions and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Supply-house price sync for thinset and membrane
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the tile supply house changes setting materials prices, the tile estimator updates the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the estimator. Needs the supply house's price sheet.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-quote from the tile walkthrough
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through the shower walls, the niche and the curb, and it drafts the tile quote before you've left the bathroom."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Booking calendar for backsplash visits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Backsplash clients pick a quote visit from your open slots and get a reminder to have the tile on site."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their calendar and which days they do quote visits.

softwareAI.name: Helper applicant screener for tile work
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tile helper applicants answer whether they've mixed thinset, run a wet saw and can lift a slab, so you only call the real ones."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the tile estimator for solo setters
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every solo tile setter gets the same 'how much for this shower?' DM. The estimator I built for one setter answers it for all of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Setters are many, solo and price-sensitive, so a small monthly tool spreads across a lot of them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Find-a-setter directory for a tile distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who buy tile at the distributor ask who can set it. A directory of their trusted setters, with quote forms, keeps that sale closing."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Tile sitting in a garage is a sale at risk of return. Distributors pay to get it installed.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Installer program site for a shower membrane maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Trained shower installers need a locator, registration for the system warranty and build guides. I've built that flow for a tile setter."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Membrane makers sell on installer training. A site that tracks trained setters is their marketing.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Tile setters' trade association member kit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every member tile setter a site template with a pattern gallery and shower page as part of membership."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want visible member benefits. One deal reaches many setters.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies rarely know how to show tilework properly. License my tile template with the pattern gallery and photo quote form ready."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep the client; you sell them the finished tile piece.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The multi-location tile and stone showroom
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each showroom location gets a page of approved tile setters by town, with a handoff that books the quote visit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Showroom chains want installed sales and fewer complaints about bad setters.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Tile setter training school enrolment site
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The tile training school or union training centre
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The tile school down the road needs a site that fills classes. Your setter client's work shows students what the trade looks like."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Training programs have budgets tied to enrolment, and the setter often teaches or hires from there.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rental bathroom refresh program for landlords
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Small landlords and property managers, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Landlords with tired tub surrounds need a simple refresh price list. One page per portfolio with a set tile spec and turnaround."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Landlords buy repeatable fixes. A fixed tile spec makes every unit the same job.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Monthly tile and setting materials price sheet
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly sheet on porcelain, thinset and membrane prices, built only from receipts tile setters share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Setters re-price constantly. Built from contributed receipts, it never claims more than the receipts show.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Course and template pack for new tile businesses
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Setters going out on their own, per pack
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Setters leaving a crew to go solo need a quote template, a tile policy and a simple site. Sell the pack your first tile client uses."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The pack is already built and tested, so each sale is nearly pure margin.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A new tile client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I keep it to one tile setter per city. {City} is covered, so the shower-and-backsplash template moves to the next town."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the tile proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The setter stuck with an old free-host site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Lots of setters have an old tile site nobody updates. I move it onto a pattern-gallery template in a week."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: They already know they need a site. A fast, cheap fix closes easily.

upsellLadder.offer: Tile site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "Tile site and care plan on one contract, so a new shower on the gallery is one text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review ask after the grout cures
upsellLadder.trigger: The first shower or backsplash finished since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "That walk-in shower client loves you right now. Let's turn every finished tile job into a review."

upsellLadder.offer: Close-up tile shoot and short reels
upsellLadder.trigger: They finish a feature wall or shower they post about more than once.
upsellLadder.line: "You posted that niche three times. Let's shoot it properly in raking light and put it at the top of the tile gallery."

upsellLadder.offer: Tile job price estimator by wall and floor area
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of form data shows the same backsplash and shower sizes asked about.
upsellLadder.line: "Most tile quote requests are a backsplash or a tub surround of similar size. The estimator answers them first."

upsellLadder.offer: Night-time tile quote assistant for DMs
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a backlog of unanswered price DMs.
upsellLadder.line: "Those midnight shower price DMs can answer themselves and book a tile quote visit."

upsellLadder.offer: Tile job schedule with cure times
upsellLadder.trigger: They take on a helper or start running two tile jobs at once.
upsellLadder.line: "Two showers at once means two sets of cure times. Let's put every tile job on one schedule."

upsellLadder.trigger: A year of tile jobs since launch, with dates on file.
upsellLadder.line: "Last year's showers are due a grout reseal. Each reminder is a small tile job and a chance at the backsplash."
